name: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder with Anti-MOG Antibodies
aliases: MOG Antibody-Associated Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder

ethnicAssociations: More common in Caucasian and Asian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for MOG-IgG Associated Disease

criteria.description: Acute optic neuritis, transverse myelitis, or acute disseminated encephalomyelitis-like episodes
Presence of serum anti-MOG IgG antibodies detected by cell-based assay
MRI findings consistent with demyelinating lesions in optic nerves, spinal cord, or brainstem distinct from MS
Negative serum anti-AQP4 antibodies to exclude classic NMO

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical presentation consistent with NMOSD plus positive anti-MOG IgG antibodies and supportive MRI findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other demyelinating diseases, especially AQP4-positive NMOSD and multiple sclerosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral or unilateral optic neuritis with severe visual loss
searchTerms: severe vision loss in one or both eyes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) causing motor and sensory deficits
searchTerms: long spinal cord inflammation causing weakness and numbness
extensive transverse myelitis with motor and sensory loss
spinal cord lesion causing paralysis and sensory changes
large spinal cord damage affecting movement and sensation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis-like brainstem or cerebral symptoms
searchTerms: brain inflammation causing sudden neurological symptoms

common.symptomName: Painful eye movements associated with optic neuritis
searchTerms: optic nerve pain with eye movement

common.symptomName: Sensory disturbances including numbness and paresthesias
Bladder and bowel dysfunction due to spinal cord involvement
searchTerms: loss of bladder and bowel control
spinal cord causing bladder and bowel problems

occasional.symptomName: Ataxia or coordination difficulties from cerebellar or brainstem lesions
Nystagmus or diplopia due to brainstem involvement
Muscle weakness or spasticity in limbs

rare.symptomName: Seizures associated with cortical demyelinating lesions
Respiratory failure secondary to high cervical spinal cord lesions
searchTerms: breathing failure from neck spinal injury
respiratory arrest due to high spinal lesion
difficulty breathing from cervical spinal cord damage
breathlessness from neck spinal cord injury

laboratory: Positive serum anti-MOG IgG antibodies by cell-based assay
CSF pleocytosis with mild lymphocytic predominance
imaging: MRI showing longitudinally extensive spinal cord lesions (≥3 vertebral segments)
Optic nerve enhancement on MRI during acute optic neuritis
Brain MRI lesions often involving deep gray matter, brainstem, or cortical regions
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible HLA associations under investigation
other: Good response to corticosteroids and immunosuppressive therapy

distinguishingFeatures: More severe and often bilateral optic neuritis
Different MRI lesion patterns with more necrosis
Presence of oligoclonal bands in CSF
Typical periventricular and juxtacortical lesions on MRI

redFlags: Rapid onset of bilateral vision loss
Longitudinally extensive spinal cord lesions on MRI
Poor response to typical multiple sclerosis treatments
references: Jarius S, et al. MOG encephalomyelitis: international recommendations on diagnosis and antibody testing. J Neuroinflammation. 2018.
Wingerchuk DM, et al. International consensus diagnostic criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders. Neurology. 2015.
Reindl M, et al. MOG antibody-associated disease: a review of clinical presentation, diagnosis, and treatment. Nat Rev Neurol. 2023.
